hardware_dossier.transmitter: 700-year-old ceramic-cavity maser transponder (Model DS-771 Mk.IV) locked to the 1,420.405 MHz hydrogen line. Its mechanical barometer reed corroded shut centuries ago during a Force-8 gale, locking its telemetry buffer into an eternal storm warning.
hardware_dossier.feedline_anomaly: The buoy hull rests high and dry on a baked white polygon salt flat where the ammonia sea evaporated four centuries ago, yet its solar-assisted trickle cell still fires a 4.2-watt packet every 90 seconds.

characters.signature_quote: [SONDE DS-771-04]: BUS 28.4V • BARO REED STUCK: FORCE-8 GALE WARNING • AMBIENT HUMIDITY 0.00% ALKALI SALT.
characters.bio: Manufactured by Pelagic & Deep-Field Telemetry Works and air-dropped into the Veyra-3 Alkali Basin in the M-33 Triangulum Spur during the First Deep-Field Survey centuries ago. Its mechanical barometer reed corroded shut in a Force-8 gale long before the ammonia sea evaporated into dry white polygonal salt crust, leaving its trickle solar-RTG bus firing a 4.2-watt gale warning every 90 seconds.
characters.language_sample_transcript: Deep-Field Survey Telemetry Unit D-S-seven-seven-one dash zero-four. Veyra-Three Basin. Barometer reed: nine-four-two millibars, locked. Warning: Force-Eight gale, six-meter swells. Ambient moisture: zero point zero zero percent dry alkali salt.
characters.phonetic_and_conlang_notes: Deep-Field Survey Telemetry Protocol: deterministic alphanumeric register readout locked to the 21-cm Hydrogen line.

worldbuilding.habitat_and_culture: A blindingly white polygonal alkali-salt desert on an uninhabited world in the M-33 Triangulum Spur (2.73 million light-years away). Nobody is out there to photograph the buoy—the only visual feed comes from the wide-angle inspection camera bolted directly to the sonde's own weathered yellow steel sensor boom.
worldbuilding.spectrum_gimmick_title: 2.73-Mly Gravitational Micro-Lens QRP (4.2W Industrial Sonde on 21-cm Hydrogen Line)
worldbuilding.hauser_commentary: Extragalactic on 1420.405 MHz (minus 180 kHz Doppler): autonomous industrial drift-sonde M33-771 (Model DS-771 Mk.IV) brought up to S4 by a Perseus gravitational micro-lens—still dutifully issuing Force-8 marine gale warnings for an ammonia sea that dried up centuries ago, while its onboard horizon camera looks out past its own yellow sensor boom across bone-dry white salt flats! Only 4.2 watts!
worldbuilding.qsl_postcard_style: Industrial Device Identification & CAD Schematic Card (Pelagic & Deep-Field Telemetry Works)
worldbuilding.qsl_animation_notes: Industrial device verification card: left panel displays the orthographic CAD engineering schematic and serial plate of Sonde DS-771 Mk.IV with blinking telemetry nodes; right panel shows its onboard horizon camera POV as the helical whip antenna fires a cyan-green 4.2W burst and an ion dust-devil sweeps the salt flat!

discovery_arc.summary: Decoded Sonde DS-771-04 frame: barometer reed stuck at 942 mbar gale warning while onboard horizon cam shows 0.00% dry polygonal salt crust.
Onboard horizon camera frame B captures fresh vehicle/foot tracks and a localized ion vortex right in front of the sonde's yellow sensor boom—and the tilt sensor resets from 34.2° to 0.0°!
